You'll collaborate closely with pharmaceutical scientists and process engineers to translate mission objectives into qualified hardware that flies in months, not years. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We take the newest and hardest problems across space, missiles, air, sensors, autonomy, and cyber, decide what is worth building, and prove it out: we build the models, break the assumptions, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. ABOUT THE JOB We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As Deputy Chief Engineer in Discovery, you lead the technical work on concepts nobody has proven, usually several at once. You learn whatever domain each one lives in and build the thing that tests it: the prototype, the test article, the demonstration. Analysis gets a concept to the point where it is worth building; building it is how we find out. You are the technical authority for the concepts you own: you set the approach, review the work, and decide, on the evidence, which concepts continue and which stop. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, build it, test it, and reach a solution. You are not hired for a particular skill set. About the Job Sentry Towers are robotic systems: motors, cameras, radars, radios, and sensor boards, running on NVIDIA Jetson compute in the field. Verifying that a system like this works means accounting for physical actuation, real sensor data, and hardware that fails in ways no unit test anticipates. We’re hiring a Senior Software Engineer to own our simulation and hardware test infrastructure and make automated, whole-system testing the default for everything we ship. A regression that escapes here does not surface on a developer’s laptop. It surfaces on a tower at a site someone has to fly to, guarding a perimeter that does not pause while we debug. You will work across both halves of the problem. Our software-in-the-loop environments are declaratively defined multi-node virtual towers, complete with a simulated ground control station, synthetic sensor feeds, and a game-engine-driven world, which lets us run whole-system scenarios in CI with no hardware attached. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM The Software Integration Environment (SIE) team builds the platform Anduril uses to test software the way it will actually be flown, driven, and fought: real binaries, running on real services, under conditions we control. We provision isolated, reproducible environments for simulation and integration testing at scale, across AWS, Azure, and on-premise. The platform is used both internally by Anduril engineers and externally by our customers. Compute was the first half of that problem. The second half is the simulated world those binaries run inside — how it gets authored, how heterogeneous simulators agree on it, and how an engineer inspects and trusts what happened during a run. That is what this role owns. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer with deep C++ and real-time systems experience to build the simulation layer of the SIE platform. This is a systems software role: you will design and write the services that let independent simulators share one world — a common clock, a common entity namespace, and a clear model of who owns what — and the tooling that lets users author, reuse, and debug the scenarios they run. This is a new area with a wide surface. You will be one of the first engineers on it, which means you will set the technical direction, make the architectural calls, and be accountable for them.
